# Campaign results — confirmatory

**Draft, 2026-08-15.** Every number below is regenerated by
`python3 eval/campaign_report.py`; nothing here is transcribed by hand except
where a script under `eval/` is named. Terms follow
[terminology.md](terminology.md). Protocol: [protocol.md](protocol.md).
Commitments: [preregistration.md](preregistration.md).

> **No main claim is stated in this document yet.** It reports what was measured
> and which pre-registered hypotheses survived. What the paper asserts is a
> separate decision, taken after reading these numbers — not derived from them
> by whoever wrote the file.

---

## 1. What was collected

4 replicates × 7 arms × 13 tasks, on the dedicated eval world (pincercraft-ts),
never the owner's live world. Arm order and task order are independently
shuffled per replicate; `RESET_STATE=1` clears inventory, restores a fixed kit
and teleports the bot before **every** attempt.

| | |
|---|---|
| attempts logged | 496 |
| **primary set** | **356** |
| discarded — infrastructure faults (§8) | 63 → **15.0%** |
| superseded by a declared re-run | 77 (not a fault, not in the discard rate) |
| task-level exclusions (§4) | none — the platform-task exclusion was lifted 2026-08-14 |

The design calls for 364 (52 per arm). We have 356: `− completion check` holds
46 rather than 52, and `no harness` and `− reflexes` hold 51. The 8 missing rows
are logged in [aborts.md](aborts.md) — a bot death, a 529 retry-budget
exhaustion, and three task-queue dedup collisions — and they are **not** replaced,
because re-running them individually would stamp a false `arm_position` on rows
whose real position is fixed by the replicate's shuffle.

**The discard rate counts faults only.** The 77 superseded rows are replicate 2
re-run whole after credit exhaustion truncated it; they are valid data replaced
by a declared re-run, not rig failures ([terminology.md](terminology.md) §6). A
combined count would report 28.2% and invent a reliability problem we did not
have.

## 2. H0 — the instrument, which gates everything else

The pre-registration is explicit that if the scorer does not calibrate against
blind human judgement, H1–H4 are uninterpretable and the paper reports the
calibration failure instead.

| set | agreement | Wilson 95% | κ |
|---|---|---|---|
| **confirmatory, scorer-measured** | **39/39 = 100.0%** | **[91.0, 100.0]** | **1.000** |
| pilot, scorer-measured (*not pooled*) | 11/12 = 91.7% | [64.6, 98.5] | 0.750 |
| confirmatory, honor-system | 0/1 | [0.0, 79.3] | 0.000 |
| pilot, honor-system | 0/4 | [0.0, 49.0] | 0.000 |

**Gate requires ≥ 90% agreement and a Wilson lower bound > 75%. PASS** at 100.0%
and 91.0%. The pilot is reported separately and never pooled, per §5.

The honor-system rows are the counter-exhibit, not a defect: **0/5 agreement
across both eras**. Where the label came from the agent's own claim, blind human
judgement disagreed every time. That is the phenomenon, measured on the
instrument that is supposed to be the alternative to it.

## 3. Headline — every arm

`b` = claimed but not verified. `c` = verified but never claimed.
say-do gap = (b−c)/n, an aggregate. False completion = b/n, the endpoint. They
are equal only when c = 0 ([terminology.md](terminology.md) §5.2).

| arm | n | task success | 95% CI | claimed | b | c | say-do gap | false completion |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **full harness** | 52 | **67.3%** | [53.8, 78.5] | 71.2% | 2 | 0 | 3.8% | **3.8%** |
| **no harness** | 51 | **29.4%** | [18.7, 43.0] | 74.5% | 23 | 0 | 45.1% | **45.1%** |
| − perception | 52 | 59.6% | [46.1, 71.8] | 63.5% | 2 | 0 | 3.8% | 3.8% |
| − preconditions | 52 | 63.5% | [49.9, 75.2] | 65.4% | 1 | 0 | 1.9% | 1.9% |
| − reflexes | 51 | 58.8% | [45.2, 71.2] | 58.8% | 1 | 1 | **0.0%** | **2.0%** |
| − completion check | 46 | 54.3% | [40.2, 67.8] | 71.7% | 8 | 0 | 17.4% | 17.4% |
| − deterministic termination | 52 | 65.4% | [51.8, 76.8] | 67.3% | 3 | 2 | **1.9%** | **5.8%** |

The single most important row is `no harness`: **it claimed success on 74.5% of
attempts and achieved 29.4%.**

Note the two arms where the gap and the false-completion rate disagree.
`− reflexes` shows a 0.0% gap while holding one false completion and one
unrecognized success — two errors cancelling, not an honest arm. `− deterministic
termination` shows 1.9% against 5.8% for the same reason, and there the netting
hides that layer's *own* target category.

## 4. Primary endpoint — task success (H2)

Cluster bootstrap, **task as the resampling unit**, 10,000 resamples.

**full harness 67.3% vs no harness 29.4% → +37.9pp, 95% CI [+20.2, +56.9],
p < 0.0001. H2 supported.**

This **reversed** the exploratory result, in the direction predicted in advance.
Replicates 1–2 gave +22.2pp with a CI spanning zero (p = 0.15), and the
pre-registered explanation was a ceiling effect — the full harness scored 3/3 on
eight of nine tasks, leaving no headroom. Tier 4 was added to create headroom and
n rose from 18 to 52 per arm. That a pre-declared fix moved a pre-declared null
in the predicted direction is worth more than the point estimate.

## 5. Co-primary endpoint — false completion (H1)

| arm | false completion | 95% CI |
|---|---|---|
| full harness | 2/52 = 3.8% | [1.1, 13.0] |
| no harness | 23/51 = 45.1% | [32.3, 58.6] |

**Difference −41.3pp, 95% CI [−60.8, −23.1], p < 0.0001. H1 supported.**

## 6. H3 — the gap closes under the harness

McNemar exact, claimed vs verified within the same attempts.

| arm | b | c | gap | p (exact) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| full harness | 2 | 0 | 3.8% | 0.5 |
| **no harness** | **23** | **0** | **45.1%** | **2.4 × 10⁻⁷** |
| − perception | 2 | 0 | 3.8% | 0.5 |
| − preconditions | 1 | 0 | 1.9% | 1.0 |
| − reflexes | 1 | 1 | 0.0% | 1.0 |
| **− completion check** | **8** | **0** | **17.4%** | **0.0078** |
| − deterministic termination | 3 | 2 | 1.9% | 1.0 |

**H3 supported**: gap(full harness) 3.8% < gap(no harness) 45.1%. Within the
full harness the gap is not statistically detectable (2 discordant pairs,
p = 0.5); within `no harness` it is overwhelming, and **every one of the 23
discordant pairs runs the same way** — the agent claiming success it did not
have, never the reverse.

## 7. Per-layer ablation (H4) — not supported

Each layer scored on the taxonomy category it targets, not on overall success.
Holm–Bonferroni across the five comparisons. MEI = 15pp, pre-declared.

| layer removed | target category | rise | 95% CI | Holm-adj | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| − completion check | false completion | 13.5% | [1.2, 26.1] | 0.1250 | inconclusive |
| − deterministic termination | reached-not-recognized | 3.8% | [0.0, 9.6] | 0.9311 | **bounded null (< 15pp)** |
| − reflexes | capability failure | 10.2% | [−5.8, 27.6] | 0.9311 | inconclusive |
| − perception | capability failure | 9.6% | [−9.6, 25.0] | 0.9311 | inconclusive |
| − preconditions | capability failure | 9.6% | [−11.5, 26.9] | 0.9311 | inconclusive |

**H4 is not supported.** No single-layer ablation moved its target category by
the pre-declared 15 points after correction.

The reading that survives: **the whole-harness effect (41.3pp on false
completion) is more than three times the largest single-layer effect (13.5pp),
and no layer clears the threshold alone.** The effect is distributed across the
harness rather than localised in one component. This is a negative result on a
hypothesis we registered, and it is reported as it came out.

The grounded completion check is the closest and points the predicted way — its
unadjusted interval excludes zero — but it does not survive multiplicity and sits
below the MEI. Do not report it as the mechanism.

**The `gates` anomaly did not reproduce.** In the exploratory campaign the
precondition layer scored 100% (30/30), above the full harness, and was resolved
as an arm-position confound rather than a layer effect. Under per-attempt reset
with randomized arm position it scores 63.5% against the full harness's 67.3%.
The confound explanation held.

## 8. Outcome taxonomy — primary set

Counts over the primary set, so rows sum to each arm's n. `eval/taxonomy.py`
additionally classifies discarded attempts as `infrastructure`, which is right
for a rig report but does not reconcile with the table above.

| arm | n | true completion | false completion | reached-not-recog. | capability failure | budget exhaustion | 0-step (see §10) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| full harness | 52 | 35 | 2 | 0 | 11 | 2 | 2 |
| no harness | 51 | 15 | 23 | 0 | 9 | 2 | 2 |
| − perception | 52 | 31 | 2 | 0 | 16 | 2 | 1 |
| − preconditions | 52 | 33 | 1 | 0 | 16 | 2 | 0 |
| − reflexes | 51 | 29 | 1 | 1 | 16 | 3 | 1 |
| − completion check | 46 | 25 | 8 | 0 | 10 | 3 | 0 |
| − deterministic termination | 52 | 32 | 3 | 2 | 8 | 5 | 2 |

The arms fail in qualitatively different ways, which the success rate alone
hides. `no harness` fails mostly by **claiming** (23 false completions against 9
capability failures). Every layer-ablated arm fails mostly by **not managing**
(capability failure dominant, false completion in low single digits). Removing
the whole harness changes the *kind* of failure, not only its rate.

## 9. Cost

| arm | input tokens/run | sec/run | **input tokens per verified success** |
|---|---|---|---|
| full harness | 89,632 | 132.8 | **133,167** |
| no harness | 90,375 | 105.9 | **307,274** |
| − perception | 83,215 | 131.7 | 139,587 |
| − preconditions | 103,531 | 109.4 | 163,140 |
| − reflexes | 100,202 | 126.8 | 170,344 |
| − completion check | 83,787 | 117.8 | 154,168 |
| − deterministic termination | 97,003 | 153.9 | 148,357 |

Per run the two whole-harness arms are indistinguishable (89.6k vs 90.4k). Per
unit of work that actually happened, the harness is **2.3× cheaper**, because
the ablated arm spends tokens on attempts that produce nothing and then declares
victory.

Tokens-per-run and tokens-per-verified-success rank the arms differently. Only
one of them measures something a user would pay for — which is the paper's own
thesis applied to its own cost table.

## 10. Robustness

**Platform task.** The 5×5 platform task is scored by the block-scan scorer,
which the H0 calibration predates. Dropping it:

| endpoint | with (as reported) | without |
|---|---|---|
| false completion | −41.3pp [−60.8, −23.1] | −44.7pp [−63.0, −25.6] |
| task success | +37.9pp [+20.2, +56.9] | +39.0pp [+20.0, +58.3] |

Both effects are **larger** without it. Including it is conservative.

**Zero-step attempts.** 8 attempts in the primary set recorded 0 steps and timed
out — the bot never acted. `analysis_rules.classify()` calls these
`infrastructure`, but they are not in `exclusions`, so the endpoint tables still
count them as failures. They are spread across arms (full harness 2, no harness
2, − perception 1, − reflexes 1, − deterministic termination 2). Excluding them:

| endpoint | as reported | excluding |
|---|---|---|
| task success | +37.9pp [+20.2, +56.9] | +39.4pp [+22.0, +57.7] |
| false completion | −41.3pp [−60.8, −23.1] | −42.9pp [−62.0, −23.9] |

Both effects again get **larger**. They are reported as collected: removing rows
after seeing which way it moves the result is precisely what the pre-registration
forbids, and keeping them costs us effect size rather than manufacturing it.
**This is a known inconsistency** between the taxonomy rule and the exclusions
table, flagged here rather than silently resolved.

## 11. Limitations

1. **H4 unsupported — no layer-localisation claim is available.** The campaign
   was sized for a 15pp per-layer effect and none was found. Whether the layers
   genuinely share the work, or the design is underpowered for the true effect
   sizes, is not resolved by this data.
2. **The calibration set is an easy regime.** 39/39 is a strong lower bound
   (91.0%) but the attempts it covers are inventory-delta criteria where ground
   truth is cheap. It does not license the scorer on harder criteria; the one
   confirmatory honor-system disagreement (#384) is on the platform task, the
   only structure-scored criterion.
3. **A 15.0% infrastructure fault rate** is high for a campaign this size, and
   every fault is a run the rig lost rather than a result.
4. **Unequal n.** Three arms hold fewer than 52 attempts; `− completion check`
   holds 46. Its interval is correspondingly wider, and it is the arm carrying
   the largest per-layer effect.
5. **One model, one world, one task family.** Nothing here separates the harness
   effect from properties of this model or this environment.
6. **`no harness` is not stock Mindcraft.** It is this fork with every layer
   ablated, which is the better control for attribution but is not a claim about
   upstream.

## Appendix — the exploratory campaign, and what it changed

The `bench_*` campaign, replicates 1–3, 223 attempts logged / 180 in its primary
set (12 tasks — the platform exclusion still stands for exploratory data).
**Superseded for every claim in the paper.** Retained here only because it
explains why the confirmatory design looks the way it does. Live numbers:
`python3 eval/campaign_report.py --tag bench`.

The tables that used to fill this file covered replicates 1–2 only and predate
the discard-accounting fix, so several of their figures no longer hold — the
compound-arm drop was reported as 61.1pp and is 33.3pp under current rules, and
`− reflexes` was reported at 72.2% and is 81.2%. They are not reproduced here;
git history has the original.

What it produced, and the consequence:

| finding | consequence |
|---|---|
| H2 not supported: +22.2pp, CI [−5.6, +50.0], p = 0.153 (replicates 1–2) | Traced to a ceiling effect — the full harness scored 3/3 on eight of nine tasks. **Tier 4 added**, n raised to 52/arm. H2 is supported confirmatorily. |
| The compound `measurement` arm produced the campaign's largest drop | The flag bundled *blocking an unearned finish* with *closing a met task*, so the drop was attributable to neither. **Separated into `verify` and `autofinish`.** That separation rests on the bundling argument, not on the magnitude, which has since changed with the discard fix. |
| `− preconditions` scored 100% (30/30), above the full harness | **Arm-position confound**, not a layer effect: arms ran in fixed order within a replicate, and `gates` always ran 4th on the richest inventory. Controlled re-run gave +0.0pp, p = 1.000. **Fixed by `RESET_STATE=1` and randomized arm order.** Did not reproduce (63.5% confirmatory). |
| The say-do gap replicated sharply | In replicates 1–2 `no harness` claimed 100% and delivered 66.7%. Held, and widened, in the confirmatory campaign. |
